thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: service=redwood-inference-api env=prod metric=p99_latency value=920ms > threshold=800ms :rotating_light:

maya: got the pager, i'm primary this slot. looking at traces now.

maya: quick check — is this across all regions or a single zone?

oncall-liaison: seeing increased tail latency for requests routed to eu-west-1 only. traffic spike from a customer batch job noted. :eyes:

jonah: thx. maya do we have KV cache pressure? last time eu-west had similar blips it was kvcache thrash.

maya: initial logs show repeated kv cache miss floods + eviction churn. putting command to inspect cache metrics:
```
# check redis kv cache hit ratio (approx)
curl -s http://metrics.redwood.internal/api/metrics?name=kv_cache_hit_ratio | jq .value
```

maya: runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-stall — follow section "evict/rollback" if hit ratio < 50% and p99 > 700ms.

sam: i'm secondary, can take on scaling tasks. propose scale up the inference pool for eu-west while we stabilize cache.

maya: agreed. sam -- scale up by +2 workers, set max pods to +30% transiently. kubectl snippet:
```
kubectl -n redwood scale deploy inference-eu-west --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy inference-eu-west -o=jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2))
```

sam: running scale now. watching pod startup logs.

incident-bot: Deployment rollout started: inference-eu-west by sam at 4471234670.

jonah: meanwhile i'll enable prefix cache fallback in the router config for eu-west so we serve slightly stale cached prefixes instead of cold KV hits. config path: /deploy/router/overrides/eu-west/prefix_fallback=true

maya: good call. also toggling short TTL for session keys to reduce eviction pressure:
```
# change TTL via feature flag
redwoodctl feature-flags set session_kv_ttl=90 --env=prod --region=eu-west
```

sam: pods are coming up. 2 added, 1 pending then ready. p99 dropping from 920 -> 560ms 1m after scale.

maya: nice. customer impact: partial for batch-heavy tenants in eu-west; API errors not observed, just high latency. I'll mark customer-impact as "degraded" in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.com/INC-2026

oncall-liaison: quick checklist for handoff (maya -> jonah):
- confirm p99 < 700ms for 10m
- verify cache hit ratio improving > 65%
- ensure scaled replicas remain stable and not autoscaled down for 15m
- post required notes in INC-2026

maya: I'm going to stay until p99 stable for 10m. if it reverts i'll escalate to infra. leaving quick ops pointers here: heatmap query, tail logs, restart steps, rollback snippet:
```
# heatmap
curl -s https://metrics.redwood.internal/query?m=p99_lat,region=eu-west | jq .
# tail logs
kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=inference-eu-west -f --tail=200
# restart single replica (graceful)
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/inference-eu-west --to-revision=$(date +%s)
# rollback to previous revision if rollout fails
kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deploy/inference-eu-west
```

jonah: noted. i'll take over if you need to step away. adding comment to INC-2026 w/ actions performed and runbook sections used.

maya: update — 10m window at 4471234699 shows p99 steady ~540ms, hit ratio 72%. leaving a final note and handing off primary to jonah in 5 mins. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sam: good job. will keep watch on autoscaler spikes.

jonah: taking primary at 4471234699. if anything flares, @maya please ping. i'll monitor next 30m and post status every 10m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 status updated -> mitigated (partial) by team at 4471234699.

maya: handoff complete. checklist done. leaving a short postmortem draft in INC-2026: root cause = kvcache churn from batch job + insufficient transient capacity in eu-west. action items: add throttling to large batch clients, tune kvcache eviction policy, and adjust autoscaler for batch spikes.

jonah: will pick up action item for autoscaler tuning. thanks.
